gloss: to let pass; to wait out; to overdo

definitions.gloss: to let pass; to wait out
definitions.explanation: To let something pass by without acting, or to wait for something unpleasant to end.

definitions.gloss: to overdo; to go too far
definitions.explanation: To do something to excess, beyond what is appropriate.

examples.japanese: {嵐|あらし}が{過|す}ぎるまでやり{過|す}ごした。
examples.english: I waited until the storm passed.

examples.japanese: {危険|きけん}な{状況|じょうきょう}を{静|しず}かにやり{過|す}ごすしかなかった。
examples.english: I had no choice but to quietly wait out the dangerous situation.
I overdid it with the drinking.

examples.japanese: {冗談|じょうだん}をやり{過|す}ごした。
examples.english: I went too far with the joke.

examples.japanese: {練習|れんしゅう}をやり{過|す}ごして{体|からだ}を{壊|こわ}してしまった。
examples.english: I overdid the practice and hurt my body.

notes: Sense 1 is the more common meaning in everyday use. The nuance is deliberately staying still or inactive while something passes. Sense 2 shares the やり{過|す}ぎる pattern of excess. Transitive verb. Collocations: {雨|あめ}をやり{過|す}ごす (wait out rain), {危機|きき}をやり{過|す}ごす (weather a crisis).
